full_judgment: 13. The Arms Act of 1878 was enacted by the then Central Government as it was thought expedient to consolidate and amend the law relating to arms and ammunition. This Statute was applicable to all the Provinces under British Administration and there was no discrimination so far as its applicability was concerned amongst British subjects within centrally administered areas in the then India. But since 1932 a departure had been made so far as Bengal was concerned when British Imperialists had to face tremendous difficulties in suppressing Revolutionary Movement in Bengal. It was with this end in view British Government inserted a new section "19A" and a proviso to section 20 in the Arms Act by the Bengal Criminal Law (Arms and Explosives) Act of 1932 (Bengal Act XXI of 1932) and later on another new section 20A was introduced in the Arms Act by Bengal Act VIII of 1934 prescribing heavier penalty. It is pertinent to note that provisions of these sections were meant only for Presidency of Bengal and not for any other parts of former British India.
